question: How many games will the 2026 World Chess Championship last?

calls.reasoning: Format: 14 classical games, first to 7.5 wins; 7-7 goes to rapid/blitz tiebreaks, which I count as games before a winner is decided (so 15 or more). The match ends at game n<14 only if the lead is at least 15-n, so the cumulative chance of finishing by game n equals P(|score diff| >= 15-n). A random-walk model with a 66-75% draw rate and an edge for Sindarov (bookmakers about 73%, Polymarket 72%; Gukesh down to 2703) gives about 10-13% finished by game 11, about 20-29% by 12, about 46-55% by 13, about 17-19% for 7-7 tiebreaks and the rest at game 14. History of 14-game matches: 11 (2021), tiebreak (2023), 14 (2024). No market on the number of games was found; Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi and bookmakers only price the winner.
calls.dossier:
- Format (worldchess.com and Wikipedia, read 2026-10-01): up to 14 classical games (120 min + 30 min after move 40), first to 7.5 points wins immediately. At 7-7: 4 rapid (15+10), then 2 rapid (10+5), then 2 blitz (3+2), then sudden-death blitz. Rest day after every 3 games.
- Schedule: Game 1 on 2026-11-24, Game 14 on 2026-12-11, tiebreaks on 12-12, at Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva.
- Players (Wikipedia, 2026): Gukesh is champion, age 20, rated about 2703 after losing 43 points in 2025. Sindarov, age 20, won the 2026 Candidates with 10/14, 1.5 points clear of Giri.
- Bookmakers (chessdom/olbg, 2026): Sindarov at about 1.36 decimal. Carlsen called Sindarov 'a pretty significant favorite'. Sindarov said recent form tells little about the match.
- Prize money: $200k per game win, which gives an incentive to play for wins.
- History of 14-game matches: 2021 Carlsen-Nepomniachtchi ended after game 11 (7.5-3.5). 2023 Ding-Nepomniachtchi went 7-7 then to tiebreaks. 2024 Gukesh-Ding was decided in game 14 (7.5-6.5) with 5 decisive games.
- History of 12-game matches: 2006, 2012, 2016 and 2018 went to tiebreaks. 2008 ended at game 11, 2013 at game 10, 2014 at game 11, 2010 at game 12.
- Mechanics: the match ends at game n (n<14) once the lead is at least 15-n (lead 2 at game 13, 3 at game 12, 4 at game 11). At game 14 any lead ends it; 7-7 goes to tiebreaks.
- Resolution: the count of games played before a winner is decided. This most plausibly includes tiebreak games, so 7-7 means 15 or more; the wording is ambiguous.
- Event window: 2026-11-24 to about 2026-12-12; as of 2026-10-01, 0% has elapsed and no games have been played.
- Searched but not found: any market or bookmaker line on match length or on a tiebreak happening; a head-to-head classical record.

calls.reasoning: Format: 14 classical games, first to 7.5 wins; at 7-7 the match goes to tiebreaks, which I count as '15 or more' (the more natural reading of 'games before a winner is decided'). The match can end at game n<14 only if the lead is at least 15-n. A random walk with ~35% decisive games and Sindarov taking ~65% of them gives ~72-75% for Sindarov, consistent with Polymarket's 0.72. It puts cumulative finish probabilities at ~3% by game 10, ~13% by 11, ~31% by 12 and ~57% by 13, with ~14% for a tiebreak. I nudged tiebreak/14 up because past World Championship matches have been cautious and drawn-out (5 of 11 since 2006 went to tiebreaks) and because a classical-only count would map 7-7 to '14'. No market on match length was found; Polymarket and Manifold price only the winner.
calls.reconciliation: No factual disputes: all three dossiers agree on the format, the schedule, the ratings shift (Sindarov ~2777 vs Gukesh ~2703) and the winner markets (Sindarov ~0.72). The disagreements were judgments: how fat the early-finish tail is, whether 13 or 14 is the mode, and how much weight tiebreaks get. I re-derived the random walk myself with an edge consistent with the market's ~0.72-0.75 for Sindarov. It supports Runs 1 and 3's thinner early tail (P(end by 11) ~13%) over Run 2's ~25%, and puts 13 and 14 close together with 14 slightly ahead. I set tiebreak at ~17%, above the model's 14%, for historical draw-stickiness. I kept a little mass on '14' to cover the classical-only reading of the resolution. The interpretation question itself cannot be settled from the dossiers.
